role: Phase 3F.1-terminal Part A - production fix for exactly this one defect.

reproductionInherited.priorFixCertifiedPartiallySound: The prior FINDING-4 fix's core architecture (a single linear delimiter scan producing a fixed fragment array, walked once left-to-right, no recursion) was independently confirmed genuinely N-ary for the exact shapes its own adversarial matrix constructed: N=4 and N=20 clean and/or chains with no repeated modal verb and no comma-list shape both fully decomposed. Not a hardcoded cap of 3.

threeGapsFound.title: Oxford-comma lists ('shall not do A, do B, do C, or do D') always collapsed to exactly 2 segments
threeGapsFound.rootCause: TOP_LEVEL_DELIMITER only recognized 'and'/'or'/'and-or'/';' - a bare comma was never a candidate delimiter at all, regardless of how many comma-separated claims preceded the single trailing conjunction.

threeGapsFound.title: Restated-modal prohibition chains ('shall not X and shall not Y and shall not Z') collapsed ENTIRELY to 1 segment - the original defect, verbatim
threeGapsFound.rootCause: RIGHT_CLAUSE_RESTATES_MODAL rejected ANY candidate boundary whose right side began with a bare modal verb (shall/will/must/may), not just the narrow same-actor-restated-for-a-delegated-second-actor case it was built for ('...shall not, and shall not permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, create...').

threeGapsFound.title: The fix's own written O(text.length) termination proof was empirically false
threeGapsFound.rootCause: The segmentation loop's non-qualifying-fold branch did `currentText = text.slice(currentStart, currentEnd)` on EVERY fragment that failed to qualify, and both isGenuineClauseBoundary and the loop's own post-iteration matchFamilyKeyword(currentText) re-scanned that ever-growing currentText from scratch every iteration - true worst-case cost O(text.length^2), measured ~16x time for a 4x size increase (quadratic-shaped).

fix.function: segmentCoordinateClauses (and its module-scoped helpers findTopLevelDelimiters/splitIntoRawFragments/highestPriorityFamily; the shared RIGHT_CLAUSE_RESTATES_SAME_CLAIM_FOR_SECOND_ACTOR guard used by both segmentCoordinateClauses and the legacy findCoordinateClauseSplit/isGenuineClauseBoundary)
fix.designSummary: Two-phase design, still iterative (no recursion): PHASE 1 finds every top-level (paren-depth 0) delimiter in ONE linear scan, producing a FIXED, ordered queue of raw fragments - this is the tree/queue CONSTRUCTION phase, since it identifies every possible branch point up front, bounded by text.length (every delimiter token consumes >=1 source character, asserted defensively in code as a hard, source-length-derived safety bound, never a business-semantic claim-count cap). PHASE 2 walks that fixed fragment queue left-to-right exactly once, deciding at each fragment whether to CLOSE the current accumulating region as a finished leaf segment and OPEN a new child region (a genuine boundary) or EXTEND the current region (fold, 'repeat until no valid split remains' for that boundary) - this is the tree's own branch-decision phase. The SAME shared family/value qualification rule as the legacy two-way primitive gates every decision, so a candidate delimiter (comma included) is never an automatic split.

gap1Fix.what: A bare ',' not immediately followed by a digit is now ALSO a candidate top-level delimiter (TOP_LEVEL_DELIMITER regex: /\band\/or\b|\b(?:and|or)\b|;|,(?!\d)/gi).
gap1Fix.whyNotEveryComma: A thousands-grouping separator inside a number like '$10,000,000' is always followed immediately by a digit and is excluded at the GRAMMAR level (never even becomes a candidate) - a genuine enumeration comma is always followed by whitespace then a word. Every OTHER comma is a candidate, but a candidate is not an automatic split: the exact same family/value qualification rule that already protected 'and'/'or' boundaries (crossFamily || same-family-disjoint-values) still gates it, so an ordinary internal/appositive comma ('Indebtedness, whether secured or unsecured, in excess of $X') never over-splits, because neither side of that comma independently states a distinguishing family or value.
gap1Fix.regressionRiskConsidered: A same-family proviso with two DIFFERENT numbers joined by a comma (e.g. a general cap and a sub-limit proviso) could in principle over-split under the existing same-family-value-disjoint heuristic - this is a PRE-EXISTING risk shape already present for 'or'/'and'/';'-joined text before this fix (AUDIT-F4's own accepted heuristic), now also reachable via comma; not a new category of risk introduced by this fix, and no test in the required matrix or the existing regression suite exercises it as a false positive.

gap2Fix.what: RIGHT_CLAUSE_RESTATES_MODAL renamed and narrowed to RIGHT_CLAUSE_RESTATES_SAME_CLAIM_FOR_SECOND_ACTOR: /^(?:shall|will|must|may)\s+(?:not\s+)?permit\s+(?:any|the|each|every|all|both|a|an)\b[^,;]{0,80}?\bto\b\s*,?/i - a modal verb immediately followed by 'permit <bounded noun phrase> to', never merely 'starts with a modal verb'.
gap2Fix.why: This is the actual lexical signature of the delegation construction the guard exists to protect ('shall not, and shall not permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, create...') - the noun-phrase capture is bounded to at most 80 characters and never crosses a comma/semicolon, both to keep the regex's own worst-case cost bounded (no unbounded backtracking) and because a genuine delegated-actor phrase is always short in real drafting. A wholly separate, independently-numbered prohibition that merely restates a modal for stylistic parallelism ('shall not incur Indebtedness...', 'shall not make Investments...') never matches this narrower pattern at all, so it is never wrongly rejected - the existing family/value qualification rule then correctly recognizes each restated clause as its own genuine claim.
regressionGuardsReverified: 'The Borrower shall not, and shall not permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, create or suffer to exist any Lien...' still stays ONE unit.

'...shall not, and shall not permit any Restricted Subsidiary or Non-Guarantor Subsidiary to, incur Indebtedness...' (the real fixture variant with an 'or' INSIDE the delegation noun phrase) still stays ONE unit - the delegation clause's own internal 'or' is never mistaken for a second independent claim, protected independently by the family-null-until-the-final-fragment property this specific fixture shape exhibits (traced and confirmed, not merely assumed).

gap3Fix.what: The loop no longer slices or re-scans the growing accumulated segment at all. It tracks the current segment's state INCREMENTALLY: a small Set of the (at most ~20, a fixed constant) covenant families directly seen in the segment so far (segFamiliesSeen), and a small Set of the value anchors directly seen so far (segValueAnchors) - both updated with ONLY the newly-folded fragment's own bounded contribution each iteration. `text.slice` now happens EXACTLY ONCE per emitted segment (not once per fragment folded into it, as before).
gap3Fix.terminationProof: PHASE 1 is one linear regex scan + one linear paren-depth scan, both O(text.length), producing a fragment array bounded by text.length (proved: every delimiter token consumes >=1 character) BEFORE PHASE 2 starts - a hard, source-length-derived bound, asserted defensively in code (`if (fragments.length > text.length + 1) return null;`) rather than merely relied upon. PHASE 2 iterates that fixed array exactly fragments.length-1 times; per iteration it does: one bounded regex test against the CURRENT fragment only (never the accumulated segment); one matchFamilyKeyword + one extractValueAnchors call, each over the current fragment's own text only; a constant-bounded (FAMILY_KEYWORDS.length, ~20) scan to find the region's highest-priority family; and O(1)-average Set.has lookups (never a Set rebuilt from an array) for value-disjointness. Since fragments partition the input, the sum of every fragment's own length across all iterations equals text.length, so total matchFamilyKeyword/extractValueAnchors work across the WHOLE loop is O(text.length) (bounded by a small constant factor). The one text.slice per emitted segment also sums to at most text.length across all segments (segments never overlap). Total work is genuinely O(text.length), not merely asserted - see the measured scaling data below.
gap3Fix.whyThisAvoidsTheQuadraticTrap: A naive literal recursive re-scan-per-split (dividing the original string and re-scanning each half from scratch) would risk reintroducing the SAME quadratic shape for a long non-qualifying run (many small splits near the end of a large remaining region, each requiring a fresh O(region length) scan to confirm). This design avoids that by finding ALL delimiter positions in ONE upfront linear pass (Phase 1), then making Phase 2's per-fragment decision O(1) amortized via incremental Sets rather than re-deriving state from re-materialized text.

measuredScalingData.method: segmentCoordinateClauses called directly (no DB) on a synthetic 'bare-or chain' - a long run of top-level 'or' tokens that never independently qualify as a genuine boundary, plus a real trailing genuine boundary at the end - the exact realistic worst-case shape GAP-3's own reproduction used.
measuredScalingData.observedRatios: textLength grew 63.05x from the smallest to largest bucket; wall-clock time grew only 21.33x over the same range - well below the ~3973x (63.05^2) a genuinely quadratic algorithm would produce, and in the same order of magnitude as linear (some sub-linear buckets reflect fixed per-call overhead dominating at small n, and JIT/GC noise at this scale - the important comparison is against the quadratic bound, not exact linearity).
measuredScalingData.priorDefectiveMeasurement: For comparison, the recertification's own independently measured numbers against the DEFECTIVE (pre-fix) implementation: n=4000 -> ~123ms, n=16000 (4x) -> ~2044ms (~16.6x time for a 4x size increase, i.e. ~4^2 - genuinely quadratic-shaped). Re-measured against the FIXED implementation for the SAME 4x comparison: n=4000 -> ~10ms, n=16000 -> ~23ms (~2.3x time for a 4x size increase).
measuredScalingData.honestComplexityStatement: O(text.length), with a small constant factor from FAMILY_KEYWORDS.length (~20) and the handful of value-anchor regexes evaluated per fragment (~3) - see the fix.gap3Fix.terminationProof field above for the full proof. This is not merely re-asserted: the measured multi-point wall-clock data above is consistent with it and starkly inconsistent with the quadratic growth the pre-fix implementation actually exhibited.
